title: Genuina principia doctrinae de statu aequilibrii et motu corporum tam perfecte flesibilium quam elasticorum

deep.reconstruction:
This page carries out Problem I of E410: find the shape of a perfectly flexible, uniform heavy string hanging between two points, i.e. the catenary. Euler uses his general intrinsic equilibrium equations for a flexible line, set up on the previous page.

Setup. The axis AX is vertical and points upward, x is the vertical coordinate and y the horizontal one. The only applied force is gravity, P = beta = B/b (weight per unit length), and Q = 0. With sin(phi) = dx/ds and cos(phi) = dy/ds, the tangential load is p = beta sin(phi) and the normal load is q = -beta cos(phi). Hence p ds = beta dx and q ds = -beta dy.

Equilibrium equations ('first case'):
- tangential: dT = beta dx;
- normal: T dphi = beta dy.

Integration.
1. The tangential equation gives T = beta x + C. The tension grows linearly with height.
2. Put dy = u dx. Then ds = dx sqrt(1+u^2), sin(phi) = 1/sqrt(1+u^2), cos(phi) = u/sqrt(1+u^2), and dphi = -du/(1+u^2).
3. The normal equation becomes -(beta x + C) du/(1+u^2) = beta u dx.
4. Separate variables: beta dx/(beta x + C) = -du/(u(1+u^2)) = -du/u + u du/(1+u^2).
5. Integrating: beta x + C = D sqrt(1+u^2)/u.
6. Hence dy/dx = D/sqrt((beta x + C)^2 - D^2). Integrating with logarithms: beta y/D = ln[(beta x + C + sqrt((beta x + C)^2 - D^2))/epsilon]. In modern form, beta x + C = D cosh(beta y/D + const).
7. Also ds = (beta x + C) dx/sqrt(...), so D ds = (beta x + C) dy, and beta s = sqrt((beta x + C)^2 - D^2) + E. Here beta s is the weight of the arc AM.

Physically, D is the constant horizontal component of the tension. Constants are fixed on the next page.
errors: 'atque ob q = 0' should read 'ob Q = 0' (capital Q, the vertical force component). This looks like a misprint in the original or an OCR confusion; the lowercase q is then computed as -beta cos(phi).
In the partial-fraction step the scan shows '+ n du/(1+uu)'; it must be '+ u du/(1+uu)'. This is a typographic or OCR slip; the subsequent integration uses the correct form.

The normal equation is written as +T dphi = beta dy, whereas q ds = -beta dy. So the 'first case' formula is evidently T dphi = -q ds under Euler's sign convention for the normal direction mr. This is consistent, not an error.
All other computations check: dphi = -du/(1+u^2), the integration of u, the logarithmic quadrature, ds, D ds = (beta x + C) dy, and beta s = sqrt(...) + E.

ideas.what: Intrinsic (tangential/normal) equilibrium equations of a flexible string, dT = p ds and T dphi = ±q ds, applied to the catenary
ideas.modern_name: Intrinsic equilibrium equations of a string (tension-curvature balance)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jakob Bernoulli / Johann Bernoulli (1690s); Euler gave the general systematic form, as discussed by Truesdell in Opera omnia II.11
ideas.where_published: E410 itself; also earlier Euler treatments of flexible lines (e.g. Methodus inveniendi 1744; Mechanica), as surveyed by Truesdell

ideas.what: Tension in a hanging uniform chain equals beta x + C, i.e. linear in height
ideas.modern_name: Tension of catenary T = w(h + a)
ideas.where_published: Standard; in E410 and earlier works

ideas.what: Integration of the catenary via the substitution u = dy/dx and logarithms; arc-length relation beta s = sqrt((beta x + C)^2 - D^2) + E
ideas.modern_name: Catenary y = a cosh(x/a) and arc length s = a sinh

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine textbook rederivation of the catenary, used to illustrate Euler's general intrinsic equations. The material is well covered by Truesdell's history of flexible and elastic bodies, and there is nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'atque ob q = 0' — the intended sense is Q = 0 (vertical component). The print shows lowercase q, likely an original misprint.
'+ n du/(1+uu)' in the image should be '+ u du/(1+uu)'; the transcription already has the correct form.
In the logarithmic formula, the denominator symbol rendered as epsilon [?] is an arbitrary constant of integration. The next page shows it equals C + sqrt(CC - DD) when x = y = 0.
